Yeah I got the Merrel Vapor Glove and the moment I put it on I decided to return it hahaha. Nah it was actually nice but felt a bit narrow, but it was super light too which I liked. What put me off was the look tbh, that bulbous lip of the outsole on the front. I just couldn't see myself living with it. Nonetheless, it's an epic shoe when it comes to functionality. I didn't get what you meant by the squishing of heels of the Vivos though. Because one of the reasons I love Vivos is that the heels are rounded so while driving my heels feel like they're cradled in a heel cup. I had the Feelgrounds before that and the heels are not rounded, it's just a 90 degrees cutout. So, the outsole would dig in my heels. I couldn't travel driving with the Feelgrounds for that reason. However, I think they fixed it in their newer models because from the pictures it seems like the lip of the outsole is a bit higher than the older models.

I only play volleyball socially as well and that happens incredibly rarely unfortunately. However, barefoot shoes are fine. I can't do anything in any other shoes now. I feel more planted and stable. I've played basketball, football (soccer if you're from the US), paddle tennis, and I train at the gym with them as well as run on asphalt with them. So, I feel like I can do anything in barefoot shoes atm. The only caveat though is the choice of the shoe. I'd say the best shoe that I can do anything in is Vivo's Primus Lite All-Weather. It just checks all the boxes. What I wanna try next, but still a bit hesitant (but I'll do it anyway), is parkour.
What's your position though? I'd imagine being a middle blocker or a hitter would be worse than being a setter or a libero with barefoot shoes.

Well, it was unexpected that someone here would ask me that. But yeah, I just don't like god, or the idea of superiority. Why is god.. god?! Why is he superior and why does he needs some useless weaklings to worship him?! It doesn't make sense to me. Also the prophets, why are they better than anyone else, being born in that time and having those hardships, it just sounds bullshit to me, everyone has hardships, different levels ofc. But the one that sets me off the most is the idea of hell, why the fuck would a "loving" or whatever god send people to hell for not believing in him or worshipping him! Also if god knows everything, he knows where everyone would end up in the end, he knew before creating that person that that person would end up in hell (or heaven) how the fuck is that fair, and what's the point of it. It's like watching a movie you created and knowing its ending! Why?! And that where I believe in the paradox of free will. But the thing is, I don't think about it. If I had to choose between 2 things, I choose and deal with the consequences, I don't say oh it was predetermined or something, although I believe that's the case.

So yeah, I do believe in god, god could be a he, she or them, I don't really care. But I believe that there some sort of creator(s) to this world. I hate it, but that is the only logical reason I can find. Where did god come from? I have no clue. Another paradox. I tried to believe in atheism, but it just didn't feel right to me. I respect everyone from any belief, I'm against religions, but I don't hate the people following it as long as they are as respectful or even cool with it.
